sources.entry: OpenBLAS - Sets run-time dispatch for a BLAS, one kernel table per microarchitecture chosen as a DYNAMIC_ARCH build loads.

summary.one_liner: OpenBLAS is an optimized BLAS (Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms) and LAPACK library, derived from GotoBLAS2 1.13, with hand-tuned kernels for many CPU architectures.
summary.what_it_does: OpenBLAS provides optimized implementations of BLAS routines, and it includes LAPACK, which can be compiled with a Fortran compiler or from an older machine-translated C version. Builds are configured through Makefile.rule or make/cmake command-line options, and the build auto-detects the host CPU unless TARGET is set to a specific model listed in TargetList.txt. With DYNAMIC_ARCH=1 a single library contains kernels for multiple x86_64, ARM64, POWER, zarch, RISC-V and LoongArch64 targets and selects one at runtime. Developers can set thread counts through OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, GOTO_NUM_THREADS or OMP_NUM_THREADS, and by calling openblas_set_num_threads at runtime. Binary packages are offered for Windows x86/x86_64 and Windows arm64. The README also covers cross-compiling, a debug build, and optional IBM MASS support on POWER.
use_cases: speed up matrix multiplication in numerical code
build a BLAS/LAPACK library for a specific CPU
ship one binary that runs on many x86-64 or ARM CPUs
cross-compile linear algebra libraries for embedded or RISC-V boards
control thread count for BLAS-backed scientific software
use LAPACK routines for linear algebra in Fortran or C
how_to_run: git clone the OpenBLAS source (default branch is develop)
make (or gmake on BSD) to build with automatic CPU detection
make TARGET=NEHALEM to build for a specific CPU model
make DYNAMIC_ARCH=1 TARGET=<oldest model> for a multi-target runtime-dispatch library
Alternatively use cmake with a separate build directory
notable: Runtime CPU detection via DYNAMIC_ARCH, selecting kernels for the host chip from one library
Broad hardware coverage: x86, ARM64 (including SVE/SME kernels), POWER, zarch, RISC-V vector, LoongArch, WASM
Includes LAPACK and can compile a C translation of it without a Fortran compiler
Cross-compilation support with explicit TARGET selection
caveats: Non-default targets need specific compilers: DYNAMIC_ARCH on riscv64 requires an RVV 1.0-capable compiler, and some POWER features need GCC 11+
Max 256 CPUs/cores by default; larger counts need the experimental BIGNUMA=1 build on Linux x86_64
Some platforms are community-supported and not actively tested (OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFly, Haiku, SunOS, AIX testing is increasingly difficult)
Setting TARGET is advised with DYNAMIC_ARCH to avoid illegal-instruction crashes on weaker hardware
keywords: matrix library for python numpy backend
compile optimized blas for my cpu
ship one library for many cpus
